It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
il_amx_13_75: Israel bought 400 AMX-13s from France between 1956 and 1967 and, lacking modern main battle tanks because of arms embargoes, sent them into the front line in the Six-Day War instead of scouting; heavy losses followed and they were soon retired. In the game it can use speed and agility to flank heavier tanks or snipe from medium to long range at weaker ones. It fires only solid APCBC shot with no explosive filler, so one-shot kills are rare; targeting the gunner or barrel and exploiting the 5-second autoloader works better. Like most light tanks, it is easily ambushed in towns. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
il_centurion_mk_5_shot: Sho't, Hebrew for "whip", was Israel's name for the Centurion Mk.5, received from Britain between 1958 and 1960 to replace Shermans that could not match the M48s and T-54s fielded by Arab armies; it performed well and proved survivable in the 1967 Six-Day War. In the game it is identical to the Centurion Mk.5/1. Its strength is neither speed, armour nor raw penetration, as its 84 mm gun trails weapons like the T-54's D-10T, but gun handling: a two-axis stabiliser and capable APDS let it fire on the move, push around corners and react to surprises without stopping. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
il_centurion_shot_kal_alef: After 1967 the Sho't's 20-pounder, dated fire control and thirsty, weak engine were clearly inadequate, so from 1970 Israel rebuilt its Centurions as the Sho't Kal with the American 105 mm M68, a stronger diesel and new fire control; the Alef was the first such standard and fought in the 1973 Yom Kippur War. In the game its Continental AVDS-1790-2A diesel gives a mobility boost similar to the Centurion Mk 10 and Strv 101, and the M68 adds stronger HEATFS and HESH rounds. The original Mk.5 hull still protects poorly, leaving it exposed even to APCR and solid shot. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
il_centurion_shot_kal_d: The Sho't Kal Dalet of 1984 was the last production version of Israel's upgraded Centurion, adding the Barak Or fire control and better-placed Blazer reactive armour; Merkavas had fully replaced it by 1992, though it trained crews until 2002. In the game it is close to the Sho't Kal Gimel but has outstanding fire control for its rank, including a thermal sight that can see through foliage. With a 105 mm gun firing HEATFS and APFSDS, it is a dangerous shooter. Acceleration is sluggish, though, and the side armour stops little more than heavy machine gun fire. It arrived in the "Danger Zone" update.
il_centurion_shot_kal_gimel: The third production upgrade of Israel's Centurion-based Sho't Kal appeared between the late 1970s and early 1980s, adding more machine guns, a ten-round smoke discharger on each side of the turret, and Blazer reactive armour across hull and turret; it left service with the other Sho't Kals in 2007. In the game it improves on earlier Sho't Kals with a laser rangefinder, smoke grenades and the potent M111 "Hetz" round, while the ERA offers welcome protection against the HEAT shells and ATGMs common at this rank. It keeps good mobility and very useful gun depression, but lacks the thermal sight of the later Dalet. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
il_eitan: Named after Operation Protective Edge, Mantak's wheeled Eitan was built to replace the M113 and entered production as an AFV in 2022, while this IFV version with a 30 mm Bushmaster II, Spike missiles and Iron Fist protection stayed a single prototype. In the game it is big and fairly quick, protected by side ERA, thin composite panels in front and an Iron Fist system that defeats most ATGMs and HEAT shells. Cannon and Spikes cover light and heavy targets alike. The crew is packed into the nose, the turret sits awkwardly far back, and the armour is no match for a tank's. It arrived in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
il_hunter_afv: Singapore's Hunter replaced the army's ageing M113 Ultras; developed from 2006 and built by ST Kinetics, it was unveiled in 2018 and entered service from 2019, with all weapons operated remotely from inside the hull and electronic systems giving the crew all-round awareness. In the Israeli tree its remotely operated turret pairs a 30 mm cannon with two Spike missiles, and the vehicle moves quickly both forwards and in reverse. Its armour, however, can be defeated by autocannons, and its large size makes it an easy target. It arrived in Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
il_leopard_2a6_hel: Greece picked the Leopard 2 after a 1998 competition and in 2003 settled on an upgraded 2A6, the 2HEL; 30 were built in Germany and 140 in Greece, entering service from 2008. In the game it stands out for extra composite armour on the hull front, like that of the Leopard 2A7V and Strv 122, and it can wear camouflage netting. Beyond that it is a standard late Leopard 2 with a 120 mm L/55 gun, potent APFSDS and modern thermals. Gun movement is restricted when aiming over the rear and sides, and an ammunition rack sits beside the driver. It arrived in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
il_m109: Israel fielded the M109 self-propelled howitzer from the late 1960s, using it to strike key enemy positions in the 1973 Yom Kippur War and again in Lebanon in 1982, before longer-ranged versions replaced the early vehicles by 2006. In the game its 155 mm HE shell is very powerful, and the short-barrelled gun, while not suited to long-range shooting, is easy to use even for beginners. It works best in support, flanking or waiting in cover to ambush, aiming at turret roofs, lower hulls or engine decks, because the shell cannot reliably defeat Cold War tanks from the front. It arrived in the "Kings of Battle" update.
il_m109a1: Rochev was the IDF name for its M109 howitzers up to the M109A2, which differed mostly internally; by 2006 only the long-barrelled M185 version remained, often with field additions such as extra machine guns and stowage boxes. In the game it is a modest upgrade on the regular M109: the M185 fires the same 155 mm shells with no extra penetration, but higher velocity makes long shots easier. A barrel-mounted 7.62 mm machine gun clears obstacles, hits unarmoured targets and helps with ranging. Thin armour and a slow reload make it fragile, but a well-placed HE shell can still kill most MBTs. It arrived in the "Air Superiority" update.
il_m113_hvms: Bardelas is Israel's name for the M113, of which it once had 6,000; this version mounts the 60 mm HVMS gun, developed by Israel after a joint project with OTO Melara split in two, and offered for several vehicles including the M113, though only Chile ever bought it, for its M24s and M50s. In the game the gun hits reasonably hard but penetrates poorly and is slow to reload for its calibre, and its aiming angles are limited and often blocked by fittings on the roof. A large crew spread throughout the hull does make it tougher to knock out than it looks. It arrived in Update 2.51 "Spearhead".
il_m113a1_tow: Giraf was the IDF name for TOW-armed M113A1s, one of many roles filled by Israel's 6,000-plus M113s, until Spike-armed versions took over. In the game it carries ten BGM-71C I-TOW missiles, flying at nearly 300 m/s to almost 4 km, plus a 12.7 mm machine gun, and 20 degrees of depression suit hull-down positions. The chassis struggles on slopes, and the thin armour can be pierced by autocannons or, on the flanks, heavy machine guns, so patient play from behind ridges or teammates is essential. It is a niche vehicle on most maps, but in the right spot it can hold an area. It arrived in the "Air Superiority" update.
il_m163_vulcan: Hovet, meaning "batsman", was Israel's name for the American M163 Vulcan, which joined the air defence command in 1975, scored its first kill in the 1982 Lebanon War and served for more than twenty years. In the game it is identical to the American version: its six-barrelled M168 cannon fires 3,000 rounds per minute, but there is no search radar and its effective range is short. The aluminium M113 chassis gives little protection, though it is nimble and quick. It arrived with the first Israeli tree in the "Wind of Change" update.
il_m48a1_patton_III: Magach, Hebrew for "battering ram", was Israel's name for its M48 Pattons, of which about 120 were in service when the Six-Day War began; more were captured from Jordan during that war, and most were later rebuilt to Magach 3 standard. In the game this M48A1 offers good mobility, solid armour and a capable 90 mm gun with HEATFS and APCBC rounds, and it works well following just behind more heavily armoured tanks and picking its shots. It has no gun stabiliser, which makes firing on the move difficult, and its tall silhouette is hard to hide. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
il_m_51: Israel's M-51 stretched the Sherman one last time: when the 76 mm M-50 proved too weak for the T-54/55, a 105 mm gun like the AMX-30's was fitted, and its HEAT shell let the IDF tackle T-55s and T-62s in 1973 despite unreliable engines and thin armour; survivors went to Chile. In the game that HEAT round defeats almost anything it meets, even the Maus, but there is no stabiliser, off-road and reverse mobility are poor, and one hit is usually fatal. Ambushes and defensive play from behind teammates suit it far better than front-line pushes. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
il_m_51_w: The M-51 (W) is the same 105 mm Sherman conversion as the M-51, built on M4A3 and M4A4 rather than M4A1 hulls; though slow, unreliable and thinly armoured, the 180 M-51s carried the most powerful gun in the IDF's tank fleet when facing Soviet-built tanks in 1973. In the game its M4A3 hull occasionally deflects a frontal shot, and a 12.7 mm pintle gun replaces the 7.62 mm one, handy against light vehicles. Otherwise it shares the M-51's lethal HEAT round, lack of stabiliser, poor off-road and reverse speed and fragility, so it belongs behind the front line. It arrived in the "Winged Lions" update.
il_machbet: Machbet, Hebrew for "racquet", was IAI and General Dynamics' upgrade of the M163 Vulcan, swapping its AN/VPS-2 radar for an infrared tracker that was more dependable and gave no warning to aircraft RWRs, and adding a launcher for four Stinger missiles; it replaced the Hovet by 1998 and guarded the Purple Line facing Syria until Israel's air defence command was disbanded in 2006. In the game it loses the Hovet's radar rangefinder but gains the optical tracker and four FIM-92 Stingers for reaching more distant targets. The M113 chassis remains thinly armoured yet nimble. It arrived with the first Israeli tree in the "Wind of Change" update.
il_magach_2: Barred from buying modern tanks directly from the US in the early 1960s, Israel arranged for 150 M48A2C Pattons via West German reparations, but Arab outrage cut deliveries to 40 before America began supplying Israel openly. In the game it is heavy next to a Leopard 1, and its armour, though no match for HEAT or APFSDS, resists APHE, APCR, HE and most 20–30 mm autocannon fire. Fully upgraded, it keeps pace with T-54/55s. The 90 mm HEAT shell kills most MBTs but does little damage once inside, so some APHE is worth carrying for flank shots on lighter targets. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
il_magach_3: Israel's first major rebuild of its M48s gave them the American 105 mm M68 gun, an M60 engine and transmission and a lower commander's cupola to face T-54/55s and T-62s; this version also wears Blazer reactive armour, added because Egypt and Syria were fielding RPGs and ATGMs in large numbers. In the game it moves like the Magach 1 and 2 but hits much harder, its HEAT and APDS rounds handling almost any opponent. ERA this early makes it unusually resistant to HEAT shells, rockets and ATGMs, and also helps against 20–25 mm autocannons without APDS. It arrived in the "Danger Zone" update.
il_magach_3_idf: Unlike the earlier Magachs, the Magach 3 was upgraded by Israel itself, gaining the American 105 mm M68 with stronger anti-tank rounds, a 750 hp engine with the Allison transmission of early M60s, and new radios and electronics. In the game this tech-tree version lacks the Blazer ERA of the premium Magach 3, but the 105 mm gun is a big step up, with HEAT-FS and APDS able to penetrate every tank at its level, though ERA on some opponents can defeat the HEAT. There is no stabiliser, yet an optical rangefinder makes accurate shooting at several kilometres possible. It arrived in the "Drone Age" update.
il_magach_5: After heavy tank losses to RPGs and Malyutka missiles in 1973, Israel took on the American M48A5, an M48A3 rearmed with a 105 mm gun partly on the strength of Israeli combat experience, as the Magach 5. In the game it plays like other M48s but with the harder-hitting 105 mm gun, though it lacks the stabiliser of later Magachs with the Sharir gun. Blazer ERA guards well against HEAT, HE and early single-warhead ATGMs like MILAN, but this primitive reactive armour, weaker even than Kontakt-1, is useless against APDS, APFSDS and big 120 or 125 mm HEAT shells. It arrived in the "Drone Age" update.
il_magach_6: Israel bought the M60 to counter the T-62's 115 mm gun, and from 1971 crews welcomed its firepower and mobility, but in the 1973 war its vulnerability to ATGMs and RPGs cost it dearly. In the game it is effectively a standard M60 that relies on its gun rather than speed or armour: 105 mm APDS can knock out most opponents in one shot, while HEAT-FS suits lightly armoured targets such as SPAA and artillery. Good gun depression rewards using ridges, but with no ERA and armour that most rounds defeat, it is better supporting from behind than leading. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
il_magach_6_rocket: In the early 1980s a Magach 6R was stripped of its Blazer armour and fitted with two Hydra-70 rocket pods beneath the gun, 34 rockets in all, as a proposed infantry-support tank, but the Israeli army turned it down. In the game it is the Magach 6R minus the ERA and plus the rockets, whose M247 HEAT warheads, together with the gun's potent M111 APFSDS, give it plenty of punch against both light and heavily armoured targets. Added in Update 2.27 "La Royale", it was the first non-premium tank in a tech tree to carry unguided rockets.
il_magach_6a: Magach 6A was Israel's modernised M60A1, with the low Urdan cupola and sometimes Blazer ERA; it fought in 1973, in Lebanon in 1982 and against insurgents before all were raised to Magach 6B standard. In the game it resembles the American M60A1 but has no gun stabiliser, so it does better ambushing and flanking than pushing, using its low profile and reasonable mobility. Its main rounds are APDS and HEAT-FS: the HEAT-FS penetrates more but copes worse with ERA and spreads less damage inside, though its focused effect can knock out key components with careful aim. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
il_magach_6b: The Magach 6B upgraded Israel's M60A1s with the RISE version of the AVDS-1790 engine, a thermal sleeve for the barrel and Merkava Mk.1 tracks, while the low Urdan cupola moved the 12.7 mm machine gun to a mount above the main gun and added an FN MAG by the hatch. In the game it plays much like the M60A1 RISE, but the low cupola removes much of that tank's weak spot, and its M111 APFSDS outperforms the American M735, at 191 mm against 164 mm at 60 degrees and 500 m. Blazer ERA helps against HEAT, though it offers no protection from APFSDS. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
il_magach_6b_gal: Since the Merkava was never going to replace every Magach, Israel gave its older 6A and 6B tanks a modern "Gal" fire control system to bring their electronics and optics up to date, and the Magach 6B Gal was later developed further into the Gal Batash. In the game Blazer ERA gives it valuable protection against HEAT shells, the many early ATGMs and rockets at its rank, and autocannon fire. Mobility is modest but not sluggish, with decent acceleration and top speed, though reverse speed is as poor as on the Soviet tanks it often meets. It arrived in the "La Royale" update.
il_magach_6b_gal_batash: The Gal Batash upgraded a handful of Magach 6B Gals with more firepower, better protection, improved optics and electronics and a 908 hp engine to offset the added weight; built for reserve units short of Merkavas, it was among Israel's most modern tanks when it appeared. In the game, like other modernised M48 and M60 derivatives, it relies on fire control and firepower, since acceleration is mediocre and reverse poor, if better than a T-64 or T-72. The turret armour handles tandem HEAT warheads, older ATGMs and autocannon fire well, but APDS and APFSDS can still find weak spots. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
il_magach_6c: Based on the M60A3, the Magach 6C gave the gunner first-generation thermal imaging through the Gal Batash fire control system, plus a late Sho't-type engine, more smoke dischargers and a laser warning sensor. In the game it lacks the speed or armour to flank or brawl, but its improved ERA stops up to 400 mm worth of tandem HEAT and ATGM penetration, and the thermal sight keeps it competitive. APFSDS, common at its rank, goes straight through, so it is best used in support, staying hull-down with its good gun depression and picking off unaware enemies. It arrived in the "Drone Age" update.
il_magach_6m: The Magach 6M, the last Israeli development of the M60A3, was essentially a Magach 6R with the Nachal Oz fire control system; crews disliked its poor reliability, and the Magach 7 soon made it obsolete. In the game its armour and mobility are weak, but modern fire control with a gunner's thermal sight keeps it competitive, and the small cupola without a 12.7 mm mount removes a favourite target for HE shells. It suits cautious play: flanking under the cover of tougher tanks like the Merkava, or sniping hull-down with the thermals, which pays off especially in downtiers. It arrived in the "Drone Age" update.
il_magach_6r: The Magach 6R combined Blazer ERA with a new AVDS-1790-2AG engine that offered more electrical power than the earlier 2A, and a later sub-variant was prepared to take the Nachal Oz fire control system. In the game it is close to the other Magach 6 variants, with ERA, weak protection against APDS and APFSDS, and better-than-average mobility and agility. Its 105 mm gun is capable and stabilised, though there is no thermal sight, and a generous supply of smoke grenades helps it screen allies or extract itself from trouble. It arrived in the "Drone Age" update.
il_magach_7c: The Magach 7C of the 1990s was the final development of Israel's M60s, swapping Blazer ERA for passive add-on armour and compensating for the weight with the 900 hp engine of early Merkavas and the Merkava Mk.2's automatic transmission; it gave way to the Merkava Mk.4 but stayed with reserve units. In the game it improves on earlier Magachs in mobility and protection, and its new APFSDS round hits hard. The appliqué armour handles APFSDS and HEAT better than the earlier ERA, which let even autocannon kinetic rounds through, but its real strength is fire control with second-generation thermals. It arrived in the "Apex Predators" update.
il_merkava_mk_1: After Britain declined to sell it the Chieftain, Israel built its own tank under General Israel Tal, whose focus on crew survival gave the Merkava its front engine and a rear hatch for evacuating crew or carrying troops. It entered service in December 1979 and first fought in Lebanon in 1982. The first home-grown vehicle in the Israeli tree, in the game it uses its front engine to soak up hits meant for the crew, though engine damage and fires are common. A strong gun, thermal sight, laser warning and ample smoke aid survival, but it is slow next to many Western tanks. It arrived in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
il_merkava_mk_1b: Conceived in 1983 as a kit to bring the Merkava Mk.1 close to Mk.2 standard, the Mk.1B applied lessons from Lebanon with integral smoke launchers and newer ammunition; most Mk.1s were converted, serving through both Intifadas and in Lebanon again in 2006 before retirement in 2014. In the game it adds the powerful M413 APFSDS round and turret smoke dischargers to the Mk.1. As on every Merkava, the front engine shields the crew but is prone to damage and fire, and a good gun, thermal sight and laser warning compensate for mobility that trails many Western designs. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
il_merkava_mk_2b_early: Lebanon in 1982 showed that more protection against shaped charges was needed, so the Merkava Mk.2 added new fire control, laser warning, a new transmission and extra turret armour, with the Mk.2B adding a thermal sight and still more armour; 580 Mk.2s were built by 1989, none exported. In the game its main gain over the Mk.1B is composite screens on the hull and turret sides that improve resistance to HEAT and ATGMs. The strong gun, laser warning, plentiful smoke and crew-shielding front engine carry over, as do the risk of engine fires and modest mobility. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
il_merkava_mk_2d: The Mk.2D was the last version of the Merkava Mk.2, fitted with modular composite armour on the hull and turret much like the Merkava Mk.4's, which could be replaced quickly when damaged, even mid-battle, and upgraded without major changes to the tank. In the game that gives it turret protection comparable to the Mk.4, the best of any Mk.2. It is at its strongest in rocky terrain, sitting hull-down with its low silhouette and well-protected turret to hold an area against attackers. It arrived in the "Winged Lions" update.
il_merkava_mk_3_raam_segol: In the 1990s, Merkava Mk.3s of a reconnaissance squadron in the 188th Armoured Brigade tested the Ra'am Sagol ("Purple Thunder") system in southern Lebanon; on detecting an ATGM launch it alerted the crew, slewed the gun at the launcher and laid smoke, but it was never adopted, the Trophy system being preferred. In the game it shows the direction of an ATGM launcher targeting the tank and leaves the response to the player. Otherwise it is a standard Mk.3, with a 120 mm gun that penetrates most tanks, good turret armour, middling mobility and a front engine that shields the crew but risks fires. It arrived in the "Alpha Strike" update.
il_merkava_mk_3b: The Merkava Mk.3, in production from 1990, brought a new suspension, a 1,200 hp engine and transmission and an Israeli 120 mm gun derived from the Rheinmetall L/44; the 1994 Mk.3B improved turret armour and the hull, and about 700 Mk.3s of all versions were built by 2002, many still serving in the reserves. In the game it is a big jump in firepower over earlier Merkavas, with the IMI 120 mm gun firing an excellent APFSDS round. The 1,200 hp Continental diesel also gives clearly better mobility than before, letting it reach key positions first in fast-moving battles. It arrived in the "Danger Zone" update.
il_merkava_mk_3c: Produced from 1995, the Merkava Mk.3C introduced the Barak Zoher fire control system with an independent commander's sight on the turret roof, giving the tank hunter-killer capability, along with extra composite inserts in the hull to guard against RPGs and ATGMs fired from above. In the game the commander's sight lets the player scan for enemies while staying hidden behind low cover, and the commander can take over the main gun to engage targets faster. Combined with the Mk.3B's armament, that makes it a thoroughly modern tank with excellent awareness, protection and firepower. It arrived in the "Drone Age" update.
il_merkava_mk_4_lic: The Merkava Mk.4 LIC (Low Intensity Conflict) adapted the Mk.4B for dense urban fighting in the mid-2000s, covering its optics, exhausts and ventilators with tough metal mesh so explosive charges could not be planted on them, improving mine protection and adding LED-tipped marker poles and a rear camera to help it manoeuvre in streets. In the game it is nearly identical to the Mk.4B, but the mine protection adds some protection to the hull against HEAT at the cost of three extra tonnes. It works well supporting the front line from hull-down positions with its powerful gun. It arrived in the "Sky Guardians" update.
il_merkava_mk_4b: The fourth-generation Merkava, developed from the late 1990s, brought new fire control with hunter-killer sights, a 10-round revolver magazine, modular composite armour on every side and a stronger engine, but its biggest advance was electronic, with screens at each crew station and a battle management system linking units; the Mk.4B entered service in 2004 and became Israel's principal tank. In the game the non-explosive reactive armour on the turret front is worth roughly 800 to 1,200 mm, enough to survive even ATGM hits, and HEAT generally struggles against it. The weight that comes with it leaves mobility behind most foreign MBTs. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
il_merkava_mk_4m: Heavy anti-tank fire in the 2006 Lebanon War led Israel to fit its Merkava Mk.4s with Rafael's Trophy active protection, whose radar detects incoming projectiles and triggers launchers that destroy them well short of the tank; the resulting Mk.4M, nicknamed "Windbreaker", entered service in the early 2010s. In the game it is the most capable Mk.4, and Trophy lets it lead assaults without much fear of ATGMs from ground vehicles or helicopters, backed by top-tier armour and firepower. The system's interceptions are limited, however, so it still should not linger in the open. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
il_mim_72_chaparral: Israel ordered the Chaparral straight after the 1973 war, using it to guard against Syrian air attack, and in 1996 bought 36 MIM-72C Improved Chaparral systems, later armed with the smokeless MIM-72E and the MIM-72G, which used the FIM-92 Stinger's seeker to resist countermeasures; the IDF retired them all in 2003. In the game the MIM-72G's flare resistance and stronger motor make it far more dangerous than the American Chaparral's missiles and hard to evade. It still lacks radar and a gun, though, and cannot hit a locked target only metres away, a real danger when helicopters get close. It arrived in the "Sons of Attila" update.
il_namer_rcws_30: The Namer heavy APC, built on a Merkava chassis, replaced the M113 in Israeli service from 2008, usually with just a machine gun or grenade launcher; in 2016 an experimental Merkava Mk.4-based version appeared with Rafael's Samson RCWS-30 turret and Spike missiles, but budget limits halted the project. In the game it is an unusual IFV, its crew and vital parts sheltered behind a massive front engine and composite hull armour. The unmanned turret carries a fast-firing 30 mm Bushmaster and two Spike-LR2 launchers that reach out to 4 km, and auto-tracking lets it engage helicopters and low flyers. Mobility is unremarkable. It arrived in the "Seek & Destroy" update.
il_namer_tsrikhon: The Namer Tsrikhon turned the Merkava Mk.4-based Namer heavy APC into a full infantry fighting vehicle with an unmanned 30 mm turret, named Tsrikhon, and Trophy active protection; unveiled in 2017, it was still being tested and gradually introduced into IDF service from 2024. In the game it builds on the Namer 30 with the Trophy system, a larger supply of 30 mm Bushmaster ammunition and extra smoke grenades, while keeping the two Spike-LR2 launchers that can hit armour at up to 4 km. Mobility remains unimpressive and its missile supply is small. It arrived in the "Storm Warning" update.
il_sabra_mk1: IMI's Sabra, named after the prickly pear, developed the Magach 7C into an export upgrade for ageing M60s, adding a 120 mm MG253 smoothbore gun, improved appliqué armour and Elbit's Knight fire control system; Turkey adopted the later Mk.II, converting 170 tanks into M60Ts between 2007 and 2009. In the game it looks much like the Magach 7C but carries a far stronger gun, a close relative of the top Merkavas' 120 mm. Its armour only holds up against some ATGMs and HEAT rounds, though, and mobility is ordinary by MBT standards. It arrived in Update 2.41 "Firebirds".
il_sholef: Soltam's Sholef ("Gunslinger") self-propelled howitzer of the 1980s sat on a reworked Merkava Mk.1 hull and carried GPS, inertial navigation and a computerised fire control system; though an IDF priority, it proved too costly and was dropped in the early 1990s, its M185 gun going to upgraded M109s instead. In the game the hull lacks composite armour but is thick and sloped enough to stop some kinetic rounds, while the big, thin turret is easy prey for autocannon IFVs. An autoloader and a potent HE shell that can destroy most tanks make it much stronger than the Rochev. It was a Battle Pass Season XVI reward.
il_spyder_aio: Rafael's SPYDER AIO, unveiled in 2022, puts SPYDER missiles, a mast-mounted search and tracking radar, an infrared search-and-track sensor and a vertical launcher on one vehicle, covering every direction out to 40 km; it has no confirmed operators but has been offered to countries such as Greece, India and Singapore. In the game it carries long- and short-range missiles and, unlike the IRIS-T SLM, needs no separate radar vehicle. With no armour at all, it relies on mobility: it can fire soon after halting, move after each engagement and even sneak behind enemy lines early on. It arrived in the "Leviathans" update.
il_ss_11_halftrack: Israel mounted French SS.11 missiles, locally called Tager, on its surplus American half-tracks, and these tank hunters met T-54s in the 1967 Six-Day War, though with little doctrine for missile use many were ignored and it is unclear whether any scored kills. In the game its manually guided missiles are slow compared with tank shells but hit very hard and steer well with practice, enough to tackle heavy Cold War tanks head-on. Its speed gets it to objectives first for ambushes. The open-topped, unarmoured vehicle offers almost no protection, and only four missiles are ready at a time. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
il_tcm_20: When the .50 calibre guns of its M45 quad mounts were no longer enough, Israel rebuilt them from 1969 with twin 20 mm Hispano-Suiza HS.404 cannons salvaged from retired air force aircraft, fitting them to M3 half-tracks and later BTR-152s; between 370 and 500 were produced during the 1970s. In the game it is a small, agile anti-aircraft vehicle whose rapid-firing cannons deal well with late piston aircraft and early jets flying low, and armour-piercing belts let it deal with lightly armoured vehicles too. Its own armour is thin. It arrived with the first Israeli ground vehicles in the "Fire and Ice" update.
il_tiran_4: Tiran, meaning "tyrant", was Israel's name for the Soviet-built tanks it captured in large numbers from Arab armies in 1967 and 1973, which helped replace its own losses; the Tiran 4 was a T-54 with modest logistical changes. In the game it offers the T-54's familiar firepower and mobility, including an APHE shell that usually destroys anything it penetrates, and its low, well-sloped armour stands up well to conventional rounds, making it a capable brawler. The drawbacks carry over too: a cramped interior, unprotected ammunition and slow turret traverse, plus a weaker M1919A4 roof gun in place of the DShK. It arrived in the "Danger Zone" update.
il_tiran_4_sh: Israel's captured T-54s, already lightly modified as Tiran 4s, were refitted in the 1970s with the same 105 mm M68 gun as the rest of its tank fleet, becoming the Tiran 4S. In the game it drives like the later Soviet T-54 and the Chinese Type 59, free of the early turret's shot traps, but the Western gun brings a different toolkit of APDS, HESH, HEAT and smoke rounds, so it fights quite differently from its Soviet and Chinese cousins. It arrived in the "Wind of Change" update.
il_tiran_6: Built to counter Western tanks like the M60, the T-62 fell into Israeli hands by the hundred in the Yom Kippur War, and many served as the Tiran 6 with an M2 Browning on the barrel and other local fittings. In the game it is essentially the Soviet T-62, with a stabilised 115 mm gun, good optics and a 50 km/h top speed. The 3BM4 APFSDS is the best all-rounder, especially against sloped plates, while 3BK4 HEAT-FS penetrates more but flies less accurately and does less damage inside. The barrel-mounted heavy machine gun keeps working even if the loader is lost. It arrived in the "Dance of Dragons" update.
il_tor_m1: Greece's Tor-M1s came from the stock of former East German equipment it bought from reunified Germany in 1991, delivered between 1992 and 1994; 21 still served with the army in 2024, with four more operated by the air force. In the Israeli tree it is identical to the Soviet Tor-M1, and its standout ability is engaging two targets at the same time. Because its only weapons are vertically launched missiles, however, it cannot fight ground vehicles or hit aircraft at very close range. It arrived in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
il_zsu_23_4: Around 60 Shilkas were captured by Israel from Egypt and Syria during the 1973 war and later fighting, but little is recorded of their Israeli service beyond limited training use, and one now stands in the Yad la-Shiryon museum. In the game it is identical to the Soviet Shilka, firing faster and with stronger ammunition than the Hovet, so it can fill the air in front of low-flying aircraft. Its cannons are only mediocre against ground vehicles, mobility is average, and like many anti-aircraft guns of its rank it has no guided missiles. It arrived in the "Fire and Ice" update.
il_zsu_57_2: Israel took an unknown number of ZSU-57-2s from Egypt and Syria in 1967 and 1973 and paraded them in Israeli markings on Independence Day, but whether they ever served operationally is disputed; Israel's armour museum says they did not. In the game its twin high-velocity 57 mm guns on a modified T-54 chassis are more of a threat to ground vehicles than aircraft, since the slow sustained fire and poor accuracy make air targets hard to hit, though a single HE shell destroys any aircraft. Mobility is good, armour very light, and the front may survive a hit or two up close. It arrived in the "Fire and Ice" update.
intruder_mk_1: Britain's premium Havoc Mk I, in the game since the open beta, is a strong all-round light bomber: fast and agile, with four forward-firing .303 Browning machine guns and four 500 lb bombs. Its speed lets it dart in and out of the target area, chase down other bombers or even work as a heavy fighter. It can stay airborne on one engine and its sturdy airframe absorbs plenty of the rifle-calibre fire common at its level, which improves its chances of making it home, while two Vickers K guns provide adequate rear defence.
it_2s1: Hungary received 144 2S1 Gvozdika howitzers from the Soviet Union and retired most by 2004 as Soviet spares dried up. It has the usual SPG traits of no armour, slow turret traverse and generous elevation, and its 122 mm shell carries less explosive than a 155 mm, though a well-placed hit still kills medium tanks. A low profile and decent mobility suit flanking and ambushes in woods or towns; against tougher tanks the cupola and mantlet are the weak spots, with barrel, tracks and engine as fallbacks. It reloads faster than an M109 but slower than most tanks. It arrived in the "Sons of Attila" update.
it_39m_csaba: Nicholas Straussler designed the 39.M Csaba from his Alvis AC2, and Hungary used it on the Eastern Front mainly for command and reconnaissance, with a 20 mm Solothurn anti-tank cannon, a coaxial machine gun and driving positions at both ends; it takes its name from a son of Attila the Hun. In the game it opens the Hungarian ground line of the Italian tree, using its speed to scout, capture points and escape, and its low profile for early ambushes. The cannon reloads quickly but lacks full-auto fire and struggles against well-armoured tanks. Even heavy machine guns can knock it out. It arrived in the "Sons of Attila" update.
it_40_43m_zrinyi_2: Inspired by the German StuG III, Hungary put a 105 mm howitzer on the Turán chassis to create the Zrínyi II assault gun; Allied bombing of the factories held output to about 72, which fought Soviet forces in the east and in defence of Hungary. In the game its low profile, reasonable frontal armour and heavy howitzer threaten almost any tank, and it inherits the Turán's decent mobility, strong reverse speed and smoke grenades. It arrived in the Italian tree's Hungarian branch with the "Sons of Attila" update.
it_40m_turan_1: Barred from tank development after the First World War, Hungary based its first medium tank on Škoda's T-21 prototype, reworking the turret, hull and suspension and adding its own 40 mm gun, thicker armour and smoke grenades; it formed the core of Hungary's tank force early in the war. In the game it moves well and reloads very quickly, and smoke plus side skirts that stop small HEAT and HE rounds aid survival. The 40 mm gun's penetration is mediocre, though, the turret is slow and it struggles up hills, while angling the armour helps one plate at others' expense. It arrived in the "Sons of Attila" update.
it_41m_turan_2: The Turán II upgraded Hungary's medium tank with a fresh turret, thicker armour and a short 75 mm gun that Bofors adapted from an old field piece; about 195 were built, reaching units only in September 1943 after delays, and though outclassed by the T-34 they could hurt Soviet tanks within 500 m. Its short gun fires strong HEAT with a quick reload, much like an early Panzer IV or the Ho-I, and with good mobility, a fast reverse and reasonable armour it is a well-balanced medium, sometimes dubbed "the Hungarian MBT". Its side skirts work as spaced armour in close fights. It was a Battle Pass Season VI reward.
it_43m_turan_3: Built to counter the T-34 and KV-1, the Turán III fitted a long 75 mm 43.M gun in a larger new turret and added much more armour to the Turán II design. It plays rather like a Panzer IV H: the gun is strong enough for even the KV-1, and an uprated engine gives excellent mobility, including 48 km/h in reverse for hit-and-run tactics. Smoke and side plates help, but the stock reload is a slow 7.6 seconds, the tall hull and cupola are easy targets, and most 57 and 76 mm guns still penetrate it, so caution pays. It arrived in the "Sons of Attila" update.
it_44m_zrinyi_1: Meant as the tank-killing counterpart of the howitzer-armed Zrínyi II, the Zrínyi I combined the Turán chassis with a Hungarian 75 mm gun based on the German PaK 40, but it never got past the prototype, which was lost when Allied bombs destroyed the production line. In the game its 75 mm gun and six rockets can knock out any tank it is likely to face, and it pairs a low silhouette with the Turán family's reasonable mobility and fast reverse. It was the 2022 Summer Quest event reward, added in the "Danger Zone" update.
it_9a33bm3: Romania received 28 Osa-AKM systems from the Soviet Union in 1985 and kept them after the end of communist rule, cannibalising some to keep others running as NATO equipment took priority; 16 were still active in 2025, with retirement expected soon. In the Italian tree it matches the Soviet Osa-AKM, hitting manoeuvring aircraft at up to 10 km and steering two missiles onto the same target at once. Its wheels make it nimble enough to surprise aircraft from unexpected positions, but the large, unarmoured vehicle is vulnerable, and its upward-angled missiles leave it nearly helpless against ground targets. It arrived in Update 2.41 "Firebirds".
it_9a35_m: Hungary received about a dozen Strela-10M systems in the early 1980s to protect its ground forces from air attack, some going to an infantry regiment at Szombathely, but they were withdrawn after the Soviet collapse and all gone by 1996. In the game it rides on the MT-LBU tracked chassis and carries eight infrared-guided missiles for short- and medium-range work. The missiles handle well enough to follow manoeuvring aircraft, and an alternative photo-contrast mode lets it acquire targets further away than infrared alone. It arrived in the "Storm Warning" update.
it_ab_41: Fiat-Ansaldo's AB 41 replaced Italy's First World War-era armoured cars, gaining a 20 mm Breda cannon once war came to North Africa; around 600 were built between 1940 and 1943, making it Italy's most numerous armoured vehicle of the period, and it earned a good name with Italian crews and was used by German units too. In the game its armour stops little more than machine gun fire, and most opponents can penetrate it with ease. Speed and firepower compensate: its 20 mm cannon with a PzGr 40 HVAP belt is deadly from the flanks, and good elevation lets it engage low-flying aircraft. It arrived in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_ab_43: Only one prototype of the AB 43, an attempt to fit a 47 mm gun to the AB armoured car, was built before the 1943 Armistice of Cassibile ended work, and its German captors made little use of it. In the game it is comparable to the German Puma and Soviet BA-11 but slower than the former, at 43 km/h, and weaker for its rank than the latter. Armour that even .50 calibre rounds pierce keeps it off the front line, so it ambushes from the flanks instead. Its main round lacks explosive filler, so shots must find the crew or ammunition. It arrived in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_ariete_amv_pt1: Italy's C1 Ariete, built by the Iveco–OTO Melara consortium at the end of the Cold War to face Yugoslav and Warsaw Pact tanks, is being modernised under the AMV programme, and this PT1 is its first prototype, focused on lifting mobility to the level of other modern MBTs. In the game the CL3143 APFSDS round comes as an early modification, which makes grinding the tank much easier. It is a strong MBT for a player who can manage its weak points, though unlike the earlier Ariete it cannot fit the WAR add-on armour kit. It arrived in the "Sky Guardians" update.
it_as_42_47: The AS 42 desert reconnaissance car, built on the AB 41 chassis but with two-wheel drive, answered North African units' calls for something like the British Long Range Desert Group's vehicles; this version mounts a 47 mm Breda 47/32 tank gun. In the game it is a fast raider: good gun depression lets it fire over crests and from steep ground, and its low profile makes it easy to stay hidden until an opponent looks away. The crew sits in the open with no real armour, so it should strike quickly and fall back to cover. It arrived in the "Fire and Ice" update.
it_as_42_metropolitana: The Camionetta AS 42, or Auto Sahariana, was built for long-range reconnaissance in the North African desert and went on to serve through the Italian campaign and with the post-war state police until 1952; this first variant carries a 20 mm Breda Mod.35 cannon. In the game it accelerates and runs quickly, letting it slip around armoured vehicles and attack them from the flanks, and an HE-filled belt makes it useful against aircraft as well. Thin armour and a crew of two mean it is easily knocked out, and enemy machine guns are a serious threat. It was part of the original Italian ground tree, added in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_aubl_74_60_70m: In 1977 OTO Melara and Israel's IMI teamed up on a 60 mm high-velocity gun meant to give light vehicles armour-piercing performance that slow HEAT rounds could not match at range; OTO Melara tried it in several prototypes, including this FIAT 6616-based AUBL/74, but buyers showed little interest. In the game it fits the Italian tree's fast vehicles well, combining excellent mobility with a stabilised gun whose APFSDS has good ballistics and penetration, though it does little damage after penetrating. It fires slowly, gun depression is poor and the armour is thin. It was handed out as a 2019 "Operation H.E.A.T." event reward.
it_b1_centauro: An Italian consortium designed the eight-wheeled Centauro in the 1980s as a fast tank destroyer packing the punch of the army's Leopard 1s; it reached service in 1992, and more than 400 were built. In the game it is quick and hard-hitting for its rank, its 105 mm OTO Melara gun firing good APFSDS, while a first-generation thermal sight, weak at long range, still makes spotting enemies easier. It has no meaningful armour and relies on changing position fast. The turret turns slowly, the reload is mediocre and gun depression is limited by the turret's placement. It arrived in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_b1_centauro_romor: For Centauros deployed to Somalia, the Italian army chose Royal Ordnance's ROMOR-A reactive armour, which proved a success largely because it could be fitted easily in the field; ten sets went to Somalia and ten more to Italy for testing. In the game this is the standard Centauro I 105 with that ERA added, improving protection against HEAT and HE without really changing how it plays, since APFSDS and APDS, even from autocannons, still go straight through. It remains a fast sniper with a capable 105 mm gun, good APFSDS and a first-generation thermal sight. It arrived in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_breda_52_autocannone: Ansaldo began developing this truck-mounted 90 mm gun in 1940 as an anti-aircraft weapon that could also fire directly at ground targets, placing the Cannone da 90/53 on a modified Breda 51 army truck; production began before testing had finished, and 120 had been delivered by May 1943 for service in North Africa and the defence of Italy. In the game it is a classic glass cannon: the 90 mm gun can deal with almost any target, frequently in a single shot, but the lightly armoured truck offers almost no protection in return. It was a reward in Battle Pass Season XIII, "Tropical Storm".
it_btr_80a_hungary: Hungary bought over 500 BTR-80s from Russia in the late 1990s, when Moscow was short of money and had surplus stock to sell, replacing its ageing BTR-60s and BTR-70s; most were later modernised with stabilisers, better optics and radios, and several dozen BTR-80As went to Serbia in 2024. In the game it does a bit of everything without mastering anything: its autocannon can cripple tanks through weak spots, kill lighter armour and SPAA, and even fire at aircraft. Good mobility and the ability to swim let it slip behind enemy lines and wreck support vehicles. It arrived in the Italian tree's Hungarian branch with the "Sons of Attila" update.
it_c13_t90: OTO Melara's modular C-13 was meant to replace the M113 and was tried with several weapon fits, including this 90 mm Cockerill gun firing HEAT and HESH to support infantry and tanks, but a crowded market left it without buyers. In the game its mobility and low profile make it an excellent scout and flanker, keeping up with or outrunning tracked and wheeled rivals. There is no real armour, though the front may deflect the odd shell, and its roomy interior lets some hits pass through harmlessly. Turret handling beats the AUBL's, but the unstabilised gun is inaccurate on the move. It arrived in the "Direct Hit" update.
it_c13_tua: The C13/TUA was OTO's 1982 tank-destroyer prototype in the C13 family, fitted with the same TOW Under Armour launcher as the American M901 ITV; no C13 version ever sold, and the programme ended in 1999. In the game it is effectively an Italian M901: the front shrugs off most autocannon fire but not anti-tank rounds, and the launcher folds down whenever the vehicle moves, so it takes time to get ready after reaching a firing spot. Because it has to sit still to aim and fire its TOW missiles, it suits patient, positional play rather than aggressive pushes. It arrived in Update 2.51 "Spearhead".
it_c1_ariete: The production C1 Ariete is a core Italian MBT that improves on the pre-series version in three ways: an unlockable WAR add-on armour kit, second-generation thermal sights for both commander and gunner, and the powerful DM53 APFSDS round. Its mobility is respectable enough to keep pace with most teammates, and players who learn to cover its weaknesses will find it a very capable tank. It arrived in Update 1.89 "Imperial Navy".
it_c1_ariete_certezza: The Ariete "Certezza" is a production C1 Ariete with two long exhausts, probably fitted for a planned Tank Biathlon entry in 2014 because the standard exhaust trails obvious black smoke; in 2020 it served on the 20th Certezza course at Viterbo, where COVID-19 restrictions stretched the training of 12 marshals to ten months. In the game this premium matches the tech-tree production Ariete apart from its camouflage net and exhausts. It fires the excellent DM53 APFSDS and the WAR kit guards the turret front against kinetic rounds, but the rest of its armour is weak, so positioning matters. It arrived in the "Hornet's Sting" update.
it_c1_ariete_preserie: The Ariete (P) represents the pre-series version of Italy's C1 Ariete, so it lacks the stronger equipment of the production tank. In exchange it faces weaker opposition, most of which it can deal with comfortably, and it moves well, while its armour proves surprisingly effective at its level. With all modifications unlocked it performs better than its modest specification suggests. It arrived in Update 1.87 "Locked On".
it_c1_ariete_pso: The PSO (Peace Support Operation) version of the C1 Ariete added composite armour blocks along the hull and turret sides, chiefly to protect the crew from RPGs, though they also proved useful against weaker APFSDS and conventional HEAT. In the game that extra weight makes it one of the slowest Arietes, but the side armour handles most autocannon fire from vehicles like the BMPs and sometimes even APFSDS. It rewards players who can live with sluggish mobility and a relatively weak front, and it makes a sensible second Ariete in a top-tier line-up. It arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
it_centauro_2: Begun in 2011, the Centauro II reworked Italy's wheeled tank destroyer after operations in Iraq, Kosovo and Somalia exposed weak protection and outdated electronics, adding a V-shaped hull against mines and IEDs, separated fuel and ammunition stowage, modern sensors and a 120 mm smoothbore with an autoloader; the first prototype appeared in 2016, and 11 pre-production vehicles had been built by 2026. In the game it is fast and agile, pairing the 120 mm gun and its autoloader with effective APFSDS, a high-quality thermal sight and a laser warning system. The trade-offs are thin armour, a large silhouette and an awkwardly placed turret. It arrived in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
it_centauro_mgs_120: OTO Melara built the Centauro da 120 in the late 1990s to trial its HITFACT turret, with a 120/45 gun and modern fire control and optics; the Italian army saw no need to rearm its 105 mm Centauros, so it stayed a demonstrator whose only buyer was Oman, but it paved the way for the Centauro II. In the game its superb mobility and quick five-second reload suit both flanking and sniping, while a stabiliser, laser rangefinder and second-generation thermals allow fast, accurate shots on the move. Appliqué armour stops autocannon and heavy machine gun rounds, but tank APFSDS and HE go straight through. It arrived in Update 1.97 "Viking Fury".
it_centauro_rgo_120: The Centauro RGO is the version of the 120 mm Centauro exported to the Royal Guard of Oman, which bought six in 2008 and three more later. Its HITFACT turret, mounting the 120/45 gun, is more likely to survive a hit than the turrets of earlier Centauros, which were a serious weak spot, and the gun fires the powerful CL3143 APFSDS, able to defeat every Russian vehicle protected by Kontakt-5 ERA. It is a premium gift vehicle introduced in the "Alpha Strike" update.
it_dardo_vcc: After the C-13 failed to win an order, Iveco and OTO Melara refined its prototypes into the VCC-80, which the Italian army adopted as the Dardo infantry fighting vehicle; 300 were ordered in 1988, cut to 200 after the Cold War, and they later served in Iraq, Afghanistan and with UN forces in Lebanon. In the game it is best used for support and flanking, scouting for teammates from a good vantage point, and its cannon is very effective against the light armour common at its rank. Unlocking the TOW-2B early lets it hit tanks from cover, though the missile's damage is inconsistent. It arrived in the "Red Skies" update.
it_fiat_6614_106sr: Fiat and OTO Melara's FIAT 6614 armoured personnel carrier first appeared in 1972 and could reach 100 km/h; one prototype carried a 106 mm M40A1 recoilless rifle, but the Italian army turned it down because it already had better 106 mm carriers and the weapon was ageing. In the game that top speed lets it flank or reach ambush positions with ease, and the recoilless rifle's HEAT round can penetrate anything it meets, with a HESH shell carrying a large explosive charge as the alternative. It can also swim, using rivers and lakes to outflank. It was part of the original Italian ground tree, added in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
it_fiat_6614_firos: This rare FIAT 6614 variant carried BPD's FIROS 6 multiple rocket launcher, which could fire HEAT-tipped FIROS 51 rockets, but the Italian high command showed no interest and none were ordered. In the game it has 48 rockets ready to fire, with good penetration, and another 96 stowed inside, while impressive acceleration and a 100 km/h top speed make it ideal for flanking. Its armour only stops small-calibre fire, so straight fights are best avoided. It was an event vehicle from the "Rocket Storm" event, held from 13 to 27 March.
